panel.text: Experimental and diagnostic settings. Some changes require a viewer restart.

text.name: experimental_preset_label
text.tool_tip: Presets hold every setting on the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs. The General, Textures and Avatar tabs are not included.

combo_box.name: experimental_preset_combo
combo_box.tool_tip: Presets hold every setting on the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs; settings a preset doesn't list are set to their defaults when it is loaded. The General, Textures and Avatar tabs are not included. Built-in presets can't be changed or deleted; Cancel undoes a loaded preset.

button.label: Load
button.name: experimental_preset_load
button.tool_tip: Set the settings of the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs from the selected preset. Settings it doesn't list go back to their defaults. Cancel undoes it.

button.label: Save as...
button.name: experimental_preset_save
button.tool_tip: Save the current settings of the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs as a new preset, or replace one of your own.

button.label: Delete
button.name: experimental_preset_delete
button.tool_tip: Delete the selected preset. Only your own presets can be deleted.

view.name: experimental_indicator_legend
view.tool_tip: The marks beside each setting are a rough guide. The circle is what the option costs in frame time when it is on (or, for a value, when it is raised): blue saves time, green costs little, yellow some, red a lot. The square is how much it improves the picture: green a lot, yellow some, grey little or nothing (options for speed, loading or diagnostics). Real costs depend on the scene and the graphics card.

check_box.label: Hierarchical screen space reflections
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderssrhiz
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Traces screen space reflections through a depth pyramid: longer, more accurate reflections at similar or lower cost, no leaking through thin objects, and a smooth fade into the reflection probes where the screen has no information. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: Cone-traced glossy reflections
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderssrconetrace
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Glossy surfaces trace one reflection ray and blur its result by the surface's roughness, instead of averaging several scattered rays. Smoother and cheaper; needs hierarchical screen space reflections.

check_box.label: Blend reflections over frames
check_box.name: ssr_temporal
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Blends the screen space reflections with the previous frames, following the camera, and changes the glossy rays every frame, so glossy reflections settle smooth instead of showing a fixed noise pattern.

text.name: ssr_resolution_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Size of the buffer opaque surfaces trace their screen space reflections into, as a share of the screen. 0.5 traces a quarter of the pixels and upsamples them with a depth and normal aware filter: much cheaper, slightly softer on fine normal map detail. Alpha and water trace every pixel. Default 1.

check_box.label: Faster sun shadow filtering away from shadow edges
check_box.name: shadow_fast_filter
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sample sun shadows with 3 lookups instead of 5 where the area is clearly fully lit or fully shadowed, and only do all 5 near shadow edges. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Stabilise sun shadow edges while the camera moves
check_box.name: shadow_texel_snap
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Snap each sun shadow cascade to whole shadow map texels, so shadow edges stay put instead of crawling and shimmering while the camera moves or turns. Costs almost nothing.

check_box.label: Order-independent transparency for blended alpha (WBOIT)
check_box.name: alpha_wboit
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Blend transparent surfaces with weighted blended order-independent transparency instead of sorting them. Removes sorting errors between overlapping glass, particles and alpha planes; stacked, nearly opaque layers such as hair can look softer than with sorting.

check_box.label: Soft sun shadows (PCSS)
check_box.name: ShadowPCSS
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Soft sun, moon and projector shadows (percentage-closer soft shadows): shadow edges are sharp where an object touches the ground and soften with the distance to the object casting them. Uses a wider, rotated filter that the shadow blur smooths out. Needs shadows on (Sun/Moon or Sun/Moon + Projectors). Costs GPU time. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: shadow_pcss_light_size_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Size of the light for soft shadows, as a multiple of the sun's real size (scaled by the sky's sun scale; the moon uses the same size). Larger values give wider, softer shadow edges away from the casting object. 1 is the real sun.

spinner.name: shadow_pcss_light_size
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Size of the light for soft shadows, as a multiple of the sun's real size (scaled by the sky's sun scale; the moon uses the same size). Larger values give wider, softer shadow edges away from the casting object. 1 is the real sun.

check_box.label: Blur soft shadow edges on screen
check_box.name: shadow_screen_filter
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With soft sun shadows on: look the shadow up with a narrow, cheap filter and blur it on the screen as wide as its soft edge, without blurring across the edges of objects. Smoother wide shadow edges for fewer shadow map lookups. Needs the shadow blur (Shadow blur size above 0). Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Smooth them over several frames
check_box.name: shadow_screen_filter_temporal
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Blend the blurred sun shadow with the last frames, following the camera, to remove the remaining grain of soft shadow edges. Dropped where another surface was seen before, and held close to the current shadow so moving shadows don't leave trails. Uses two more screen sized buffers.

check_box.label: Sun shadow bias from the surface's slope
check_box.name: shadow_slope_bias
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Measure how steep each surface is from the depth of the pixels around it, instead of from its normal map, when keeping sun shadows from shadowing their own surface. Removes shadow acne and leaks on bumpy, normal mapped walls and floors, and lets the fixed bias below be smaller so shadows sit closer to the objects casting them. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: shadow_slope_bias_constant_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Share of the fixed sun shadow bias and offset kept while the bias follows the surface's slope. Lower values put shadows closer to their casters; raise it if flat surfaces facing the sun show speckles. Default 0.5.

spinner.name: shadow_slope_bias_constant
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Share of the fixed sun shadow bias and offset kept while the bias follows the surface's slope. Lower values put shadows closer to their casters; raise it if flat surfaces facing the sun show speckles. Default 0.5.

check_box.label: Merge shadow draw calls
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowmergedbatches
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends the opaque shadow casters of each shadow pass as fewer, larger draw calls. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in scenes with many objects.

check_box.label: Cache static far shadows
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Keeps the shadows of buildings and terrain in the two far sun shadow maps between frames and only redraws moving things into them. Needs 'Snap sun shadows to texels' (FSRenderShadowTexelSnap). Uses one extra depth buffer per far shadow map.

text.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachesunangle_label

spinner.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachesunangle
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the static far shadow cache, the far shadows follow the sun in steps of this many degrees, 0 to 2. Larger steps redraw the cache less often under a moving sun.

check_box.label: Keep far shadow maps still in a busy view
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachestable
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs Cache static far shadows. Lets the far shadow cache be reused while avatars move in view: a far shadow map stays where it is while its part of the view still fits inside it, and objects that only change colour or texture no longer make the cache redraw. Shadows look the same. 'Log shadow batch statistics' shows how often the cache is reused, and why it is redrawn.

check_box.label: Draw sun shadow cascades in one pass
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowsinglepass
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends buildings, objects, rigged mesh and alpha masked surfaces to the sun shadow maps once instead of once per shadow cascade; the graphics card copies each to every cascade it reaches. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs a graphics card and driver that can pick the viewport in the vertex shader (most NVIDIA and AMD cards with current drivers); otherwise nothing changes. Uses one extra depth buffer the size of the four sun shadow maps.

check_box.label: Keep still projector shadows
check_box.name: fs_fsperfspotshadowcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A projector's shadow is only redrawn when something it shows can have changed: the light moved or changed, objects in its cone were added, removed or changed detail, or an avatar or moving object is inside its cone. Otherwise the last shadow is kept, and it is redrawn at least once a second anyway. Saves the culling and drawing of every shadowed projector that only lights static scenery.

check_box.label: Keep projector shadows of static objects
check_box.name: fs_fsperfspotshadowsplit
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs Keep still projector shadows. A projector with avatars or moving objects in its cone keeps the shadow of its static objects and terrain, and each frame only culls and draws the avatars, attachments, animesh, moving objects, trees and grass over it. Saves most of the main thread time of projectors lighting people. Uses one extra depth buffer per shadowed projector. Translucent parts of avatars stay grey in coloured projector shadows.

Works up to the second sun shadow split (the nearest few tens of metres). Uses two extra textures the size of the shadow maps (about 8 MB each at 1920x1080 with shadow resolution 1) and redraws transparent objects into the two nearest shadow maps. Needs sun shadows.

check_box.label: Keep decoded textures on disk (faster loading on return visits)
check_box.name: decoded_texture_cache
check_box.tool_tip: Stores the pixels of decoded textures so places you return to load them without JPEG2000 decoding. Uses several times more disk space than the regular texture cache. Cleared together with the texture cache.

combo_box.name: decoded_texture_cache_mode
combo_box.tool_tip: A region can take several GB of decoded textures. Listed regions only keeps just the regions named below. Current region only keeps what you see where you are, so relogging or moving around the same region reuses it, and drops it once you are somewhere else. Places visited before only keeps textures that were already in the texture cache, so a first visit writes nothing.

line_editor.name: decoded_texture_cache_regions
line_editor.tool_tip: Region names, separated by commas. Their decoded textures are kept on any visit, not dropped when you leave, and removed last when the cache is full.

text.name: decoded_texture_cache_min_size_label
text.tool_tip: Textures smaller than this (larger side, in pixels) decode quickly enough and are not kept.

check_box.label: Store uncompressed (faster loading, about 1.5x the disk space)
check_box.name: decoded_texture_cache_uncompressed
check_box.tool_tip: Decompressing is most of the cost of loading from the decoded cache, and texture pixels only compress to about 65%. Applies to newly stored textures.

check_box.label: Decode the most important textures first
check_box.name: prioritize_texture_decodes
check_box.tool_tip: Decodes textures in order of importance instead of request order, so what is in front of you sharpens first after a teleport or while moving. Decodes for textures nothing waits for anymore are skipped.

check_box.label: Run texture decode and cache threads at low priority
check_box.name: low_priority_texture_threads
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Texture decoding and caching only use CPU time the main and render threads leave free. Smoother frames while a scene loads, but loading can take longer on CPUs with few cores.

check_box.label: Use the video memory the driver reports for the texture budget
check_box.name: use_live_vram
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. On NVIDIA and AMD, textures are reduced when the GPU itself is running out of video memory, counting everything else using it, instead of using a fixed share of it. Has no effect when the texture memory limit is set manually.

text.name: texture_bias_soft_zone_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How far below the texture memory target textures start being reduced, a little at a time, so memory levels off before it runs out instead of dropping detail all at once. 0.1 starts at 90% of the target. 0 waits until the target is reached.

panel.text: Start reducing textures before memory is full

spinner.name: texture_bias_soft_zone
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How far below the texture memory target textures start being reduced, a little at a time, so memory levels off before it runs out instead of dropping detail all at once. 0.1 starts at 90% of the target. 0 waits until the target is reached.

check_box.label: Streamed texture uploads (PBO)
check_box.name: fs_fsperftextureuploadpbo
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Copies newly loaded textures to the graphics card asynchronously, which can reduce stutter when many textures arrive at once. Only has an effect when textures are not already created on a background thread (usually AMD and Intel graphics). Needs OpenGL 4.4.

text.name: fs_fsperftextureuploadbudgetmb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Spreads bursts of newly loaded textures over several frames so they don't all land in one frame, uploading the most important ones first. Lower is smoother but textures appear more slowly. 0 = no limit. 16 is a good start.

spinner.name: fs_fsperftextureuploadbudgetmb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Spreads bursts of newly loaded textures over several frames so they don't all land in one frame, uploading the most important ones first. Lower is smoother but textures appear more slowly. 0 = no limit. 16 is a good start.

check_box.label: Recover stalled texture downloads automatically
check_box.name: texture_fetch_self_heal
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. If textures sit waiting for a download slot while no texture downloads are actually running, give the slots back so loading continues. Logged under Texture.

check_box.label: Reduce textures hidden behind other objects first
check_box.name: fs_fstexturepriorityhiddenfaces
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Textures seen only on surfaces the occlusion test has found hidden behind other objects for a few seconds are treated like textures off screen: when video memory runs short they are reduced first, and they no longer get the close-up boost. Surfaces that come back into view count as visible again at once. Has an effect only while textures are being reduced to save memory.

text.name: fs_fstexturepriorityhiddengrace_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How long, in seconds, a surface must stay hidden behind other objects before its textures are treated like textures off screen. Longer keeps textures sharp behind things passing in front of them.

spinner.name: fs_fstexturepriorityhiddengrace
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How long, in seconds, a surface must stay hidden behind other objects before its textures are treated like textures off screen. Longer keeps textures sharp behind things passing in front of them.

check_box.label: Choose PBR texture detail from the material's texture repeats
check_box.name: fs_fstexturepriorityglftscale
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Choose the detail of PBR (GLTF) material textures from the repeats of the material's own texture transform, which is what draws them, instead of the face's legacy texture repeats, which PBR materials don't use. Textures repeated many times load less detail, stretched ones more.

check_box.label: Load the textures of small avatar parts (eyes, lips, nails) early
check_box.name: fs_fstextureavatarsmallparts
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Textures load in order of how much of the screen they cover, so tiny avatar parts like eyes load last and are the first to be dropped when video memory runs short, leaving grey eyes. With this on, the textures of attachments in view count as at least the size below, so they load early and stay loaded. Uses a little more video memory.

text.name: fs_fstextureavatarsmallpartssize_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The smallest texture size, in pixels, the textures of attachments in view are loaded at. 128 keeps eyes sharp at a conversation distance.

spinner.name: fs_fstextureavatarsmallpartssize
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The smallest texture size, in pixels, the textures of attachments in view are loaded at. 128 keeps eyes sharp at a conversation distance.

check_box.name: repair_animations
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Every 2 seconds, restarts animations other avatars should be playing but are not, because they failed to load, were dropped, or a looping animation got stuck stopped. Only that avatar's broken animations are restarted, up to 5 times each. Logged under FSAnimRepair.

check_box.label: Retry sooner for avatars stuck as a cloud
check_box.name: avatar_cloud_fast_retry
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. When another avatar is missing its shape or body textures, ask the region for its appearance again after 15, 30 and 60 seconds, instead of only every 2 minutes.

check_box.label: Ask again when an avatar's appearance arrives without a shape
check_box.name: avatar_retry_empty_appearance
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. When the region sends another avatar's appearance without a shape, ask for it again right away (at most every 10 seconds) instead of waiting for the cloud timeout.

check_box.label: Ignore out of order appearance updates
check_box.name: avatar_drop_stale_appearance
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. During an outfit change, appearance updates for another avatar can arrive out of order. Ignore one that is older than the last applied, if it arrives within 10 seconds of it. Logged under Avatar.

button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Login" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Load my outfit and attachments sooner after login
check_box.name: fs_fsfastselfrez
check_box.tool_tip: Shortens the time other people see your avatar half loaded after you log in. The viewer starts loading your outfit as soon as your inventory list arrives instead of after the loading screen's wait, and asks the region for up to four attachments at a time instead of one. Attachments that take a long time to rez on the region side are not affected. The log gets a list of when each attachment was requested and arrived.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_perf_heading_avatars
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Avatars" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Keep avatar ranking steady while object updates arrive
check_box.name: perf_avatarrankhysteresis
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Only re-rank avatars for impostors and loading when one is added, removed or reseated, or when its on-screen size changes enough. Without this, every object update in the region re-sorts all avatars every frame.

check_box.label: Reuse rigged mesh joint matrices until the skeleton moves
check_box.name: perf_riggedpalettecache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Build each rigged mesh's joint matrix palette once per skeleton update and reuse it in every render pass (camera, shadows, probes), instead of rebuilding it for each pass.

check_box.label: Skip unchanged attachment bounding box updates
check_box.name: perf_attachmentextentscache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Only push a rigged attachment's bounding box into the scene tree when the avatar's bounds actually changed.

check_box.label: Build rigged mesh skinning matrices on the avatar workers
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelskinpalettes
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With 'Update other avatars on worker threads' on, build the skinning matrices of each avatar's rigged attachments on its worker too, right after its pose, instead of on the main thread while drawing. The main thread then only checks that no joint moved since, and builds them itself if one did. Saves main thread time with many avatars around.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_fs_heading_skin
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Skin" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Subsurface scattering on avatar skin
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinsss
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Softer, more lifelike skin under strong light: light bleeds slightly through and around the skin, with a reddish falloff at shadow edges and around ears and fingers. Applies to avatar surfaces weighted by how skin-like their colour is. Needs HDR. Turning it on or off rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinsssstrength_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much of the diffused light replaces the lit skin. Only the light is diffused: skin texture and highlights stay sharp, so 1 (the physical look) does not blur the face. 0 turns the scattering off.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinsssstrength
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much of the diffused light replaces the lit skin. Only the light is diffused: skin texture and highlights stay sharp, so 1 (the physical look) does not blur the face. 0 turns the scattering off.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinsssradius_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Scale of the skin diffusion profile. 1 is measured human skin (red light spreads about 6 mm, green and blue stay sharp); 1.5 reads well at portrait distance; larger looks softer and waxier.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinsssradius
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Scale of the skin diffusion profile. 1 is measured human skin (red light spreads about 6 mm, green and blue stay sharp); 1.5 reads well at portrait distance; larger looks softer and waxier.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinssstint_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much further red light scatters than green and blue. 1 gives the reddish glow of human skin at shadow edges, 0 a neutral soft blur.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinssstint
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much further red light scatters than green and blue. 1 gives the reddish glow of human skin at shadow edges, 0 a neutral soft blur.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinssstonematch_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. 0 applies scattering to every avatar surface (rigged mesh and the system body), 1 only to surfaces whose colour looks like skin, which keeps it off most clothing. Lower it for non-human or unusually coloured skins.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinssstonematch
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. 0 applies scattering to every avatar surface (rigged mesh and the system body), 1 only to surfaces whose colour looks like skin, which keeps it off most clothing. Lower it for non-human or unusually coloured skins.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinssstranslucency_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sunlight shining through thin skin lit from behind: ears, fingers and nostrils glow red when the sun is behind the avatar. 1 is the physical amount, 0 is off. Needs sun shadows (thickness is measured in the sun shadow map); the radius above also scales how thick skin can be and still glow.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinssstranslucency
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sunlight shining through thin skin lit from behind: ears, fingers and nostrils glow red when the sun is behind the avatar. 1 is the physical amount, 0 is off. Needs sun shadows (thickness is measured in the sun shadow map); the radius above also scales how thick skin can be and still glow.

check_box.label: Only Bakes on Mesh is skin
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinbakesonly
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Only rigged mesh faces that show your avatar's bakes (Bakes on Mesh) count as skin. Mesh clothing, hair, jewellery and animesh attachments (ears, tails) are never treated as skin, whatever their colour; the system avatar still is. Applier skins (textures put on the body directly, not Bakes on Mesh) need this off, and are then judged by colour as before.

check_box.label: Detect skin by its material too
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskindetectmaterial
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Judge what is skin by its material as well as its colour: skin is non-metallic with medium roughness, while most cloth is rougher and jewellery metallic or very glossy. Keeps scattering off beige clothing and lets the colour test take in pale, very dark and fantasy skins. The system avatar's bakes have no material, so there colour still decides. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskintonerange_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With material detection on: how far the skin colour test opens up. 0 is the human tone range, 1 takes any hue and very pale or very dark skin; the material test keeps clothing out instead.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskintonerange
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With material detection on: how far the skin colour test opens up. 0 is the human tone range, 1 takes any hue and very pale or very dark skin; the material test keeps clothing out instead.

check_box.label: Show what counts as skin (debug)
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskindebug
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug view: avatar surfaces are tinted green as far as they count as skin, red where the colour test turns them down and blue where the material test does. Replaces the scattering while on.

check_box.label: Two-lobe skin highlights
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskindualspecular
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Skin shines with two highlights in one: a sharp one from its oily surface and a broad, soft one from fine wrinkles and pores, as film and game character shading does. Applies to the sun and local lights, at skin's own reflectance and with the same total brightness as one highlight. Legacy skins without a specular map get a skin highlight too. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinspecularmix_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much of the skin's highlight is the sharp lobe; the broad, soft lobe gets the rest. 0.85 is the usual split; lower looks softer and more matte.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinspecularmix
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much of the skin's highlight is the sharp lobe; the broad, soft lobe gets the rest. 0.85 is the usual split; lower looks softer and more matte.

check_box.label: Warm shadow edges and creases on skin
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinwarmshadows
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Creases, eye sockets and the soft edges of shadows on skin go warm red instead of grey, as light scattered under the skin fills them red first. Works on ambient occlusion and the sun's shadow. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinwarmshadowstrength_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How warm skin creases and shadow edges get. 0 leaves them grey, 1 is strongly red; 0.5 is subtle.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinwarmshadowstrength
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How warm skin creases and shadow edges get. 0 leaves them grey, 1 is strongly red; 0.5 is subtle.

check_box.label: Backlit translucency from local lights
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskintranslucencylocal
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Local lights (club lights, lamps, projectors) behind thin skin shine through it: ear rims and fingers glow red when a light is behind them. Point lights have no shadows, so how thin the skin is gets estimated from how strongly it curves; cheeks and the back of the head stay dark. Uses the backlit translucency strength above. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Soft rim sheen on skin
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinsheen
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A faint soft glow along the edges of skin seen at a grazing angle, as the fine hair on skin (peach fuzz) catches the sun and the sky light. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinsheenstrength_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How strong the rim sheen on skin is. Low values read as soft skin, high ones as velvet.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinsheenstrength
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How strong the rim sheen on skin is. Low values read as soft skin, high ones as velvet.

check_box.label: Skin colour bleeds into the scattering
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinalbedosplit
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Part of the skin colour goes into the scattering blur instead of all of it after: the colour of freckles, lips and makeup bleeds a little into the skin around them, as under real skin. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinalbedosplitamount_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much of the skin colour goes in before the blur: 0 none (as without the option), 1 half of it (the square root, as GPU Gems 3 recommends).

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderskinalbedosplitamount
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much of the skin colour goes in before the blur: 0 none (as without the option), 1 half of it (the square root, as GPU Gems 3 recommends).

check_box.label: Keep reflected light out of the skin
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinenergy
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Light the skin's oily surface reflects as highlight does not also enter the skin: scattered light and backlit translucency are dimmed toward the edges of the face, where the surface reflects most, so rims do not glow brighter than the light allows. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Cheaper scattering for distant faces
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskintaplod
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Faces more than a metre or two away use a shorter blur (3 samples a side instead of 7) with the same overall spread. Saves about half of the skin scattering cost in crowds with no visible difference at that size. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_fs_heading_hair_and_transparency
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Hair and transparency" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Two-pass hair and layered rigged alpha
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderhairtwopass
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws alpha-blended rigged mesh (hair, layered clothing) as a depth-sorted solid core and a blended soft fringe, so inner layers stop showing through outer ones. Costs roughly two extra draws of rigged alpha. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: fs_fsrenderhairalphathreshold_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Alpha at or above which hair counts as solid and is depth sorted. Lower sorts more of each strand but hardens soft edges; higher keeps edges soft but sorts less.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderhairalphathreshold
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Alpha at or above which hair counts as solid and is depth sorted. Lower sorts more of each strand but hardens soft edges; higher keeps edges soft but sorts less.

check_box.label: Hybrid order-independent transparency (hair and glass)
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderalphahybridoit
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The solid part of all alpha (hair, glass, particles; at or above the threshold above) is depth sorted per pixel, and the soft rest of all of it is blended order independently. Stops hair showing through or cutting holes into glass and other alpha. Replaces the two options above in the main view while on. Costs an extra draw of all alpha, and alpha is no longer GPU driven. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

button.name: reset_fs_heading_avatar_occlusion
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Soft occlusion around avatars" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Soft occlusion around avatars
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderavatarocclusion
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars darken the ambient light around them: the ground under their feet, a wall they stand by, the sofa they sit on, the avatar next to them. Each frame a few rounded shapes are fitted to the skeletons of the nearest avatars and their shade is worked out exactly, so it also works at night, indoors and with ambient occlusion or shadows off. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsrenderavatarocclusionstrength_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How dark the occlusion around avatars gets, 0-1.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderavatarocclusionstrength
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How dark the occlusion around avatars gets, 0-1.

text.name: fs_fsrenderavatarocclusionshadow_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A broad soft shadow each avatar casts against the open sky above it, on the ambient light only (so mostly seen in shade, indoors and at night). 0 keeps only the occlusion close around the avatar.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderavatarocclusionshadow
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A broad soft shadow each avatar casts against the open sky above it, on the ambient light only (so mostly seen in shade, indoors and at night). 0 keeps only the occlusion close around the avatar.

text.name: fs_fsrenderavatarocclusionmaxavatars_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many of the nearest avatars get it. Each one costs GPU time on the pixels around it.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderavatarocclusionmaxavatars
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many of the nearest avatars get it. Each one costs GPU time on the pixels around it.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_perf_heading_scene
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Scene" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Re-sort transparent faces without rebuilding geometry when the camera turns
check_box.name: perf_alpharesortonly
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. When the camera turns, re-order only the transparent faces of each group for correct blending, instead of rebuilding the group's geometry.

check_box.label: Spread geometry rebuilds over frames and defer off-screen ones
check_box.name: perf_rebuildtimebudget
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Limit how long geometry rebuilds may take each frame and rebuild groups and particles that are off screen only once they come into view.

check_box.label: Fit shadow maps using the camera's visible objects
check_box.name: perf_shadowpointcloudfromcull
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Work out the shadow map bounds from the objects the camera already found visible, instead of searching the scene again for every shadow cascade.

check_box.label: Sort sun shadow casters once for all cascades
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowsharedstatesort
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the shared sun shadow cull (RenderShadowCullMode 1), the geometry rebuilds and the collection of each object group's draw calls run once per shadow update instead of once per cascade; each cascade only takes the groups in its own frustum. Shadows look the same; saves main thread time in busy scenes. Does nothing with RenderShadowCullMode 0.

check_box.label: Faster occlusion queries (NVIDIA)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfrepresentativefragmenttest
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Lets NVIDIA Turing and newer graphics cards stop drawing an occlusion test box as soon as one pixel of it is found visible, which makes the hidden-object checks cheaper. Visibility results stay the same. Has no effect on other graphics cards.

check_box.label: Leave transparent faces without glow out of the glow pass
check_box.name: fs_fsperfalphaglowskip
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Transparent faces get drawn a second time for glow whenever any face near them has glow, even when they have none themselves. Skip that second draw for faces without glow; it adds nothing to the picture.

check_box.label: Test for hidden objects after foliage, avatars and animesh are drawn
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderocclusionafteropaque
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The occlusion test that skips hidden groups of objects runs after every opaque surface is drawn, so alpha masked surfaces (foliage, fences), grass, trees, avatars and animesh hide what is behind them too. Draws less in busy scenes. Something revealed by a moving avatar or a swaying plant can show up a frame late.

check_box.label: Light particles cheaply (fog and smoke)
check_box.name: fs_fsrendercheapparticles
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Smoke, fog and other particles take the ambient light of the sky probe instead of searching the nearby reflection probes, one sun shadow sample instead of a filtered set, and the four local lights nearest the camera instead of seven. Thick fog, which stacks many large particles on every pixel, costs much less on the graphics card. Fog can look slightly different near local lights and inside buildings with their own reflection probes.

check_box.label: Light the transparent parts of distant avatars cheaply
check_box.name: fs_fsrendercheapavataralpha
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The transparent parts of other avatars farther away than the distance below (hair, lace, sheer clothing, PBR blend) are lit like cheap particles: the light of the sky probe instead of the nearby reflection probes, one sun shadow sample instead of a filtered set, and the four local lights nearest the camera instead of seven. Fog stays the same. Your own avatar, nearby avatars and HUDs keep the full lighting. Costs less on the graphics card in crowded places; distant hair can look slightly different near local lights and inside buildings with their own reflection probes.

text.name: fs_fsrendercheapavataralphadistance_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars farther from the camera than this many metres have their transparent parts lit cheaply; nearer ones keep the full lighting.

spinner.name: fs_fsrendercheapavataralphadistance
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars farther from the camera than this many metres have their transparent parts lit cheaply; nearer ones keep the full lighting.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_perf_heading_lightingandreflections
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Lighting and reflections" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Look for nearby lights 10 times a second
check_box.name: perf_lightrescanthrottle
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Rescan the scene for the nearest local lights 10 times a second, or when the camera moves, instead of every frame.

check_box.label: Skip mirror cube faces that cannot be seen
check_box.name: perf_heroprobeskiphiddenfaces
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Do not render the sides of a mirror's reflection cube that face away from the mirror surface.

check_box.label: Skip the second mirror probe data update in each pass
check_box.name: perf_probeuniformcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Do not update the mirror (hero) probe data a second time in each render pass; the reflection probe update already includes it.

check_box.label: Batch local light drawing
check_box.name: fs_fsperfbatchedlocallights
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws point lights in a few instanced calls instead of one call per light, cutting CPU time where hundreds of lights are visible (clubs, cities). Lighting should look the same. Spotlights and projectors are unchanged. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Batch projector drawing
check_box.name: fs_fsperfbatchedspotlights
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws projectors (spotlights) that are not casting shadows in a few instanced calls per projector texture instead of one call per light, and draws the ones the camera is inside of over their light volume instead of the whole screen. Cuts CPU and GPU time in crowds full of projector facelights. Lighting should look the same; shadowed projectors are unchanged. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_fs_heading_threading
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Threading" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Cull sun shadow maps on worker threads (casters found per map only)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelshadowcull
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Works out which objects fall into each sun shadow map on several CPU cores at once instead of one map after another on the main thread. Shadows look the same; saves main thread time in busy scenes. Only works with Shadows > Find sun shadow casters set to Separately per map: with Once for all maps there is a single search already, and this does nothing.

check_box.label: Check worker shadow culls against the old cull
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelshadowcullverify
check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Also runs the old shadow cull and writes any difference to the log. Slower; only for testing.

check_box.label: Build object geometry on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelgeometry
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Fills the vertex data of rezzing and changing objects on several CPU cores instead of only the main thread. Reduces hitches on region arrival, teleports and heavy rezzing. Looks exactly the same as when off.

check_box.label: Verify threaded geometry (slow, debug)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelgeometryverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug aid: builds the geometry a second time on the main thread and logs any difference to the threaded result. Costs more than it saves; for testing only.

text.name: fs_fsperfparallelgeometryminverts_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A geometry rebuild uses the worker threads only when it has at least this many vertices; smaller ones are built on the main thread, where waking the workers would cost more than it saves.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfparallelgeometryminverts
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A geometry rebuild uses the worker threads only when it has at least this many vertices; smaller ones are built on the main thread, where waking the workers would cost more than it saves.

check_box.label: Animate avatars on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelavatarupdate
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Evaluates the animations of all visible avatars of a frame in parallel on worker threads instead of one after another on the main thread. Helps most in crowded places. Your own avatar stays on the main thread.

check_box.label: Verify parallel avatar animation
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelavatarupdateverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug check: recomputes the avatar joints serially after the worker threads and logs any difference. Costs extra CPU time, only for testing.

check_box.label: Cull the main view and reflection probes on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelmaincull
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Works out which objects are in view (main camera and reflection probe updates) on several CPU cores at once instead of only on the main thread. The scene looks the same; saves main thread time in busy scenes.

check_box.label: Check worker view culls against the old cull
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelmaincullverify
check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Also runs the old view cull and writes any difference to the log. Slower; only for testing.

check_box.label: Build render lists on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsort
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Collects the draw lists of each camera (main view, shadow cascades, probes) on worker threads in postSort. Same result as before, less main thread time in busy places.

check_box.label: Verify parallel render lists
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsortverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug: also builds the render lists serially and logs any difference. Slower; for testing only.

text.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsortmingroups_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Views with fewer visible groups than this build their render lists on the main thread, where the worker hand-off would cost more than it saves.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsortmingroups
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Views with fewer visible groups than this build their render lists on the main thread, where the worker hand-off would cost more than it saves.

check_box.label: Texture priorities on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparalleltexturepriority
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Computes how sharp each texture needs to be (face screen areas and texture virtual sizes) on worker threads instead of the main thread. Helps in busy places with many textures loaded.

check_box.label: Verify parallel texture priorities
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparalleltexturepriorityverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug: also computes texture priorities the old way and logs any difference. Costs more than either alone.

check_box.label: Disk cache lookups on a separate thread
check_box.name: fs_fsperfdiskthread
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Looks assets up in the disk cache on a separate low priority thread instead of the main thread, and reads them once there so the main thread's later read comes from memory. Cached animations go through the same lookup. Helps against hitches when content arrives in bursts and the cache is on a slow disk or scanned by antivirus software. A cached asset becomes ready about a frame later.

check_box.label: Free object geometry on a worker thread
check_box.name: fs_fsperfbackgroundvolumefree
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Frees the geometry of objects that go away (a region leaving view, objects changing detail level) on a worker thread instead of the main thread. A region going out of range frees thousands of shapes at once, which took a few hundred milliseconds of the frame.

check_box.label: Run audio (OpenAL) on its own thread
check_box.name: fs_fsperfaudiothread
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Make every OpenAL call on an audio thread of its own instead of the main thread. A call that waits inside OpenAL (its locks, the mixer, an output device being reopened) then can't hold up a frame. Sounds start up to a few milliseconds later. Takes effect after a restart.

text.name: fs_fsperfopenjpegbuffercachemb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Builds that decode textures with OpenJPEG only (not Kakadu). How much of the decoder's large working buffers each texture decode thread keeps for its next decode, in MB, instead of handing them back to Windows and getting them back fresh every time. Saves the bursts of page faults that make the whole computer sluggish while many textures decode at once (logging in, arriving somewhere). 0 turns it off. Takes effect after a restart.

panel.text: OpenJPEG buffers kept per decode thread (MB)

check_box.label: Draw shadow casters with multi-draw indirect
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivendraws
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends the opaque buildings and objects of each shadow map to the graphics card as one multi-draw call instead of one call per object batch, from a copy of their positions kept in video memory. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Works together with 'Draw sun shadow cascades in one pass'. Needs OpenGL 4.3 (most NVIDIA, AMD and Intel cards with current drivers; not macOS); otherwise nothing changes.

check_box.label: Verify multi-draw shadows (slow)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivendrawsverify

check_box.label: GPU-driven PBR surfaces
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbr
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws static opaque PBR (GLTF material) surfaces with a few large multi-draw calls out of a shared vertex arena instead of one draw call each. Looks the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs OpenGL 4.3. Uses up to the arena size below of video memory. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: Bindless PBR textures
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrbindless
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With GPU-driven PBR surfaces: uses bindless textures (GL_ARB_bindless_texture) so surfaces with different materials share one draw call. Looks the same; saves more CPU time. Not used where the driver doesn't support it properly. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven PBR surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven PBR surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: GPU-driven legacy surfaces
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenlegacy
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws static opaque non-PBR surfaces (simple, alpha masked and fullbright) with a few large multi-draw calls out of a shared vertex arena, with bindless textures, instead of one draw call and several texture binds each. Looks the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs OpenGL 4.3 and bindless textures (NVIDIA GPUs only). Uses up to the arena size below of video memory. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenlegacyarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenlegacyarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: Group PBR and legacy material draws
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrgroupruns
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to GPU-driven PBR surfaces and GPU-driven legacy material surfaces: draws them grouped instead of in the stock order. PBR: every surface with bindless textures in one multi-draw, the others one run per material. Legacy materials: every GPU-driven surface in one multi-draw. The surfaces drawn the old way follow. Far fewer draw calls and texture binds in busy scenes. Only where two surfaces lie at exactly the same depth can the other one show.

check_box.label: GPU-driven legacy material surfaces
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterials
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws static opaque surfaces with legacy normal or specular maps (or shine on a material) with a few large multi-draw calls out of a shared vertex arena, with bindless textures, instead of one draw call, several texture binds and material settings each. Looks the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs OpenGL 4.3 and bindless textures (NVIDIA GPUs only). Uses up to the arena size below of video memory. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterialsarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy material surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterialsarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy material surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: Draw alpha tested shadow casters with multi-draw indirect
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenshadowalpha
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends the alpha tested shadow casters (leaves, fences, grass, cut-out textures, alpha masked PBR materials) of each shadow map to the graphics card as one multi-draw call with bindless textures, instead of one call and several texture binds per object batch. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Works together with 'Draw sun shadow cascades in one pass'; checked by 'Verify multi-draw shadows'. Needs OpenGL 4.3 and bindless textures (NVIDIA GPUs only); otherwise nothing changes. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenshadowalphaarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the copy of the alpha tested shadow casters' vertex data may use, 16 to 2048 MB. Casters that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenshadowalphaarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the copy of the alpha tested shadow casters' vertex data may use, 16 to 2048 MB. Casters that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: Rigged mesh joint matrices in one buffer per frame
check_box.name: fs_fsperfriggedpalettebuffer
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Write each rigged mesh's joint matrices once a frame into one buffer that every program, pass and shadow cascade reads, instead of uploading them to each program that draws the mesh. Saves main and render thread time with many avatars around; nothing looks different. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: GPU driven draws for rigged meshes
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenrigged
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draw the opaque rigged meshes of the G-buffer pass (bodies, clothes, attachments) as a few multi-draw calls, like the GPU driven paths above do for static objects, instead of one draw call each with its own state changes. Needs the joint matrix buffer. Saves main and render thread time with many avatars around; nothing looks different. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: GPU driven draws for alpha blended objects
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenalpha
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. NVIDIA only. In the alpha pass, draw runs of consecutive plain alpha, fullbright alpha and legacy material alpha draws that share their shader and blend mode as one multi-draw call each, in the same order, so blending stays exactly as before. Rigged ones too with the joint matrix buffer and GPU driven rigged draws on. Saves main and render thread time with many avatars around; nothing looks different. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: GPU-driven draws: upload ring
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenuploadring
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to every GPU-driven option above. Their per draw data goes into a few large buffers that take turns over three frames, instead of each pass asking the driver for 4 to 5 new buffers every time it draws. With the render thread off and OpenGL 4.4 the buffers are written directly. Less driver work; nothing looks different. The FSGPUDrivenUpload log line shows what it does.

check_box.label: GPU-driven draws: one matrix table per view and frame
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivensharedmatrices
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to every GPU-driven option above. The passes of a frame that draw with the same camera (opaque, rigged and alpha; the passes of one shadow map) share their table of object matrices, so each object's matrices are worked out and sent to the graphics card once instead of once per pass. Saves main thread time in busy scenes; the same math, so nothing looks different. The FSGPUDrivenUpload log line shows what it does.

check_box.label: GPU-driven draws: keep built passes while the scene holds still
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenbuildcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to the GPU-driven shadow caster, legacy and legacy material draws (not rigged). A pass that is given the same objects as in the last frame draws the commands it built then again instead of building them anew; only its texture handles and copies are checked and its matrices looked up again. Saves main thread time while you and the scene hold still, most of all in busy scenes; a pass whose objects changed is built as before, so nothing looks different. The FSGPUDrivenBuild log line (with the GPU-driven statistics on) shows how often it helps.

check_box.label: GPU occlusion culling for GPU-driven objects
check_box.name: fs_fsrendergpuocclusionculling
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs GPU driven draws for PBR objects; also culls what the GPU-driven legacy and material passes draw. In the main view, the graphics card leaves out static objects that are hidden behind what is already drawn: it first draws what was visible last frame, then tests every other object's box against that depth and draws the ones that turned out visible, so nothing pops in late. Saves graphics card time in dense scenes with walls and buildings in front of other objects; little in open views. Rigged meshes are tested with their avatar's bounds, generously padded (never your own avatar's). Alpha, shadows, reflection probes and mirrors are drawn as before. Turning it on rebuilds the scene's geometry once. The FSGPUOcclusion log line shows how much it culls.

check_box.label: Merge post-processing passes
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermergepostpasses
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws post-processing passes that can be one as one full screen pass, with the same math: the sun rays (or underwater rays) together with the volumetric projector light when both are on, and the vignette inside the lens effects pass when both are on. Saves a full screen pass for each pair, about 0.05 to 0.2 ms of graphics card time at 1440p. The picture stays the same apart from the last bit of rounding.

check_box.name: fs_fsperfdsatexturebinds
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws bind their textures with one call that names the texture unit, instead of switching the active unit first: about one OpenGL call fewer per texture bound. Only on OpenGL 4.5 (not macOS). Off: the standard path.

check_box.label: Rebuild nearest objects first
check_box.name: fs_fsperfrebuildnearestfirst
check_box.tool_tip: When geometry updates (level of detail changes, new objects) can't all be done in one frame, do the ones in view and nearest the camera first, so the objects around you sharpen before distant ones. Off: the standard order.

check_box.label: Decode cached objects on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfthreadedobjectupdates
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While objects around you are created from the object cache (arriving somewhere, logging in, turning around), the ones coming up next are decoded on worker threads: their shape parameters and their texture faces. The main thread then only applies them, at the same moment and in the same order as before, and decodes anything the workers haven't reached yet itself. Updates sent straight from the region (movement, changes, removals) are handled as before. The result is identical; the gain is small.

check_box.label: Build prim shapes for a new level of detail on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfthreadedgeometry
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. When a prim switches to a level of detail whose shape hasn't been built yet (arriving somewhere, moving the camera through a build), the shape is built on a worker thread instead of the main thread, and the prim keeps its current detail for one more frame meanwhile. Sculpts, meshes, flexible prims, HUDs and what you are editing are handled as before. Off: the standard path.

check_box.label: Re-check settled textures less often while the camera is still
check_box.name: fs_fsperftextureupdateslice
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While the camera stands still, a texture that is already loaded at the sharpness it needs and isn't on anything moving has its priority worked out on one pass of the texture sweep out of every few instead of on every pass. Textures still loading, sharpening or shrinking, avatar, UI and sculpt textures, projector textures and textures on moving objects keep the normal rate, and so does everything while the camera moves or turns, during a teleport and after the texture memory limit tightens. Saves main thread time in a still scene with many textures.
